newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Leningrad region plans to get credit rating.
newsitem.headline: Russia Leningrad region plans to get credit rating.

text.p: Lenigrad region plans to receive an international credit rating by the end of the year with the help of Goldman Sachs, though it does not yet plan to issue a Eurobond, a regional official said on Monday.
Deputy Governor Sergei Susekov told Reuters Goldman would work with the administration. "We have agreed with the American firm Goldman Sachs," he said. "It will prepare the region."
But Susekov said Leningrad region, surrounding St Petersburg in northwestern Russia, would not hurry the process since it did not plan to issue foreign bonds soon.

It recently dropped plans to issue a Eurobond in favour of a $100 million four-year syndicated credit from a group of 25 European banks to be received by mid-September. It also plans a municipal bonds issue to cover the budget deficit.
"If we get the syndicated credit and issue municipal bonds, the total volume of borrowing will be about $200 million," Susekov said. "We are unlikely to need more."
He said the international credit would help the region to get a credit rating equal to the sovereign one.
Standard & Poor's assigned Russia a BB- rating, Moody's Ba2 and IBCA BB+.
